doc.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

title: Meeting Wynton Marsalis in 1987 and the early years in his band
summary: Gordon recalls Marsalis visiting his school in February 1987, his initial skepticism, and the growth of working in Marsalis's band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. I’ve seen you on numerous programs and you’ve been pretty well recorded so far. Your meeting with Wynton was pretty fortuitous.

It was. I remember the day that I met him was in February of 1987. And someone said Wynton Marsalis is going to come by the school. And all the guys that were really into jazz, and it wasn’t very many but everyone knew who Wynton Marsalis was because I believe at that time he had won Grammys in classical and jazz music. And it was like man, Wynton’s coming to the school. Wynton’s coming. I was like okay, whatever. I mean not that — I had heard about him but I was into listening to Louis Armstrong. I said well this is a young cat, he can’t possibly be playing this, I was like Wynton Schmitten. And I got to chance to meet him. He was a nice guy, very down to earth, just a cool person, a great person to hang with. And then after I began to work with him a couple of years later he remained the same, just a great person, he was a great teacher, he was never really — a lot of people used to ask is he like a work horse? Does he make you practice? No. He never says anything about practicing. You know you get on the bandstand and you hear him play and when he does his thing it’s like okay [scats], back to the basics. I mean and my experience in that band was one of, it was a great growth period for me because everyone wanted to be better. They were always striving to be better. We were always talking about what they could do to make their solos and their presentation better. And we talked about it all the time. And I haven’t really had that experience since. But it was a great growing situation for me.
